root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening: removing closure or obstruction and thereby making something accessible, evident, available, or decided.
root_idea.development: From physical opening and release, the semantic range extends to disclosure, provision and other granted openings, judgment, victory, and requests for such outcomes.

senses.definition: To open, unlock, or remove a physical closure, making a door, object, or passage accessible.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes opening doors, containers, and other closed things; the passive Quranic uses describe something becoming opened.

senses.definition: To open up or grant access to blessings, provision, relief, or other favorable circumstances.
senses.usage_conditions: Often construed with عَلَى; the opening may be figurative, as when prosperity or blessings are made available.

senses.definition: To disclose, explain, or make known something hidden, obscure, or previously inaccessible.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction فَتَحَ عَلَيْهِ may mean to inform, teach, or acquaint someone with something; it can also refer to explaining a difficulty.

senses.definition: To judge or decide between parties, settling a disputed matter.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with بَيْنَ in the construction “to judge between”; the related active participle and noun occur in this judicial sense.

senses.definition: To grant victory over an enemy, conquer, or overcome.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of laying a country or adversary open; it may describe God granting victory or a people conquering territory.

senses.definition: To open repeatedly, extensively, or in multiple places; in the passive, to be opened wide or fully.
senses.usage_conditions: Form II conveys an intensified or multiplicative opening; the Quranic occurrence concerns gates being opened.

senses.definition: To seek or ask for victory, aid, or triumph over an enemy.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences use the form for seeking or requesting victory; the request may be directed to God or expressed as a challenge.

senses.definition: To seek a decisive judgment or a divinely granted opening or resolution.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran-focused discussion also records judgment and a beginning of good among the possible objects of seeking فتح; this sense is interpretive rather than a separate inflectional meaning.

senses.definition: One who judges or decides between parties.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural occurs in the expression “the best of those who judge,” in a context of asking for a decision between disputing groups.

senses.definition: Victory, aid, or conquest granted over an opponent or territory.
senses.usage_conditions: Depending on context, فتح denotes triumph, successful overcoming, or conquest; it is frequently rendered “victory.”

senses.definition: A judgment, decision, or decisive settlement of a dispute.
senses.usage_conditions: In judicial contexts فتح means the resolution by which a matter between parties is decided.

senses.definition: A divinely granted opening of benefits, knowledge, guidance, or other good.
senses.usage_conditions: In interpretations of the Quranic noun, the opening may refer not only to conquest but also to knowledge, guidance, and access to favorable outcomes.
As a divine epithet, it denotes the one who decides between disputants and settles their matter.

senses.definition: The Opener who opens the gates of sustenance, mercy, and other benefits.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a divine, figurative extension of opening and making available what was closed or inaccessible.

senses.definition: Keys, or means of access and opening.
senses.usage_conditions: مَفَاتِح may be the plural of مِفْتَاحٌ, a key or instrument of opening, and in figurative use denotes means by which something inaccessible is reached.

senses.definition: Repositories, treasuries, or hoards of wealth.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural may also derive from مَفْتَحٌ, a repository or place where things are kept; this reading is especially relevant to the Quranic reference to Qarun’s possessions.

senses.definition: Opened wide, opened up, or made accessible.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic feminine form describes something whose openings or gates have been opened; the Form II pattern can suggest an extensive or repeated opening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand that something be opened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A constructional extension of the basic transitive verb, especially with a door or other closure as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be so exceptional that no comparable person or thing is encountered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom لَا يُفْتَحُ العَيْنُ عَلَى مِثْلِهِ, literally “the eye is not opened upon his like.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open a conduit so that water runs through it for irrigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of opening a channel to conduct water to cultivated land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an opening between the legs or to part the legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily construction reported as equivalent to making a cleft or separation between them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To part the toes or incline their ends toward the upper rear part of the foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The report is tentative and is explicitly noted as possibly confused with a different root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have wide openings at the teats, said of a she-camel, ewe, or she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-descriptive usage concerning the breadth of the teat openings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grant, permit, allow, or make something unrestricted for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with the beneficiary marked by لِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fortunate or favored by circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive figurative construction describing the acquisition of good fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For God to bestow abundant first rains upon people or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression in which opening is associated with the arrival of beneficial rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prompt a reciter or prayer leader by supplying words he has forgotten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers to reciting the missing words to someone who is unable to utter them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act as an aperient or remove bodily obstructions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical usage of Form II and its active participle, especially of medicines that open the bowels or clear obstructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To address someone first.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is especially noted of addressing a king or other person of high status before he initiates speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin a dispute, debate, or controversy with someone, or summon him before a judge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III expresses reciprocal engagement in argument or litigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bargain with someone without giving him anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported commercial usage distinguished from the verb used when something is actually given.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse with one’s wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative or euphemistic construction; no narrower object-class restriction is inferred.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a thing easy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative usage of the Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be liberal or generous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare poetic usage reported from classical verse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open or burst open, said of a blossom or calyx.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive Form V describes natural opening and disclosure of a flower.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To boast of one’s wealth, learning, or accomplishments, making a vain display of them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage in speech or conduct; it may be construed with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To converse together in a suppressed or confidential voice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction describing speech kept from others’ hearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open or become open, said especially of a door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VII verb is the intransitive or quasi-passive counterpart of opening a closure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be removed from before or over something so that it is disclosed or exposed to view.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes one thing becoming uncovered when another is removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open or commence something, including commencing prayer or beginning a period with an event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VIII verb is used of beginning prayer, beginning with a particular utterance or matter, and commencing a year or season auspiciously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, demand, or ask for the opening of a gate or other closure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited expression concerns seeking the opening of the gate of Paradise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to explain the Quran.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which the Quran is the object of the request for explanation; it is distinct from the Quranic Form X requests for victory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to prompt a reciter by supplying forgotten words.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers to the imam’s request for prompting and is linked to فَتَحَ عَلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or request judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form X usage distinct from seeking military victory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conquest, especially the conquest of Mecca; by another usage, the Day of Resurrection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional applications of يوم الفتح rather than the ordinary verbal-noun sense alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Means of subsistence or provision by which God gives aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal extension of opening and provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or early rain, especially the first rain of a season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of rain falling upon the land; the plural form is also connected with the corresponding rain-related noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Running water from a spring or other source, including water conducted through an opened channel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for flowing or channelled water, including irrigation water for which a conduit has been opened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where the tang of an iron arrowhead enters the shaft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical anatomical or weapon-making term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The red, sweet, round fruit of the nabʿ tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific botanical and food term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide, open, or large and wide, said of a door or a bottle with a wide or unstoppered mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective of the measure فُعُلٌ functioning with the sense of something opened or open.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opening, gap, or intervening space.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun synonymous with a gap or interval between things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gain, profit, or increase obtained in trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare commercial noun synonymous with رِبْحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular bird, including a reddish or black bird distinguished by its tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This zoological term is distinct from the verbal and divine-epithet uses of the same root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The office or function of a judge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of appointment to judicial office.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Litigation, altercation, or disputed proceedings between two parties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural construction describes disputes or altercations between two people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conqueror.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use derived from opening a territory by force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide or ample, said of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing spaciousness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The commencement or first part of something; specifically, the opening chapter or opening portion of a Quranic chapter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: الفاتحة is conventionally the opening chapter of the Quran because recitation begins with it; فواتح القرآن denotes the opening portions of its chapters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conduit or channel for water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal instrument or place term related to opening a passage for water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means that removes an impediment or enables an activity, such as ritual purification as the key to prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional metaphor based on a key’s enabling access to what follows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A faculty or means of access to eloquence, difficult meanings, and forms of knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: مفاتيح الكلام is a figurative expression for gifted command of speech and understanding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular brand or mark placed on a camel’s thigh and neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock-marking term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Opened, unclosed, or unlocked, especially a door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participle used adjectivally of something whose closure has been removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light or bright color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source marks this sense as probably post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A term applied to a fat she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal term unrelated to the plural meaning “keys.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act, place, or time of opening or commencing; an opening portion or beginning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote a beginning generally and, in Quranic usage, an opening portion of the Quran.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bursting or opening vehemently with rain, said of a day of clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of clouds or a day releasing heavy rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boasting or making a vain display of one’s possessions, learning, or accomplishments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative noun; its Arabic status is explicitly disputed in the source.

cautions: مَفَاتِحُ is explicitly ambiguous between a plural of مِفْتَاحٌ, “keys,” and a plural of مَفْتَحٌ, “repositories or treasuries”; the public form preserves both analyses.
فَتْحٌ in 48:1 is discussed with several Quran-focused interpretations, including victory and an opening of knowledge or guidance; the artifact records these without treating them as identical.
The reported toe-related usage of فَتَحَ is retained but marked tentative because the lexical source suggests possible confusion with another root.
The reported noun فُتْحَةٌ meaning boasting is retained as a rare, source-disputed usage.
